    # If batch is a tuple or list, recursively call add_batch on each element
    if isinstance(batch, (tuple, list)):
        batch = [add_batch(b) for b in batch]
    
    # If batch is a dictionary, recursively call add_batch on each value
    elif isinstance(batch, dict):
        batch = {k: add_batch(v) for k, v in batch.items()}
    
    # If batch is a torch.Tensor or numpy.ndarray, add a new dimension at the zeroth position
    elif isinstance(batch, (torch.Tensor, np.ndarray)):
        batch = batch.unsqueeze(0)
    
    # If batch is of any other type, convert it to a torch.Tensor and add a new dimension at the zeroth position
    else:
